idea_name: KAN spline-edge next-bar return sensor with readable curves
mechanism: Map each closed bar to four features (1-bar return, RSI, ATR/price, MA slope), normalize into the spline domain, then predict next-bar return with a single KAN layer: y=sum_i phi_i(x_i) where each edge phi is a cubic B-spline (De Boor-Cox) linear in coefficients and fit by ridge least-squares (no GD). Live indicator histograms the forecast and draws the four learned edge curves; EA thresholds the prediction and sizes stops with ATR.
data_needed: OHLC for return and MA slope; RSI; ATR; training history of feature rows + next-bar returns; ridge lambda; prediction threshold.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15 (train ~3000 bars; OOS 2026.01.01–2026.06.01 real ticks).
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an additive neural next-bar sensor whose per-feature response curves are directly inspectable (flat=ignored, bent=nonlinear use)—a white-box alternative to opaque MLP weights.
quote: A cell whose curve slopes down from left to right says the model expects that feature to bend the forecast lower as it rises. A cell whose curve is nearly flat says the model found little use for that feature.

idea_name: Relative ATR and MA-slope as KAN volatility/trend inputs
mechanism: Feature builder feeds the KAN with x2=ATR/close (relative volatility) and x3=(MA_t−MA_{t−1})/close (price-normalized slope) alongside return and RSI, so the same learned curves sense how volatility level and short trend slope bend the next-bar forecast.
data_needed: ATR handle, fast MA handle, closes; shared feature class for train/live.
why_new_for_mis: Packages relative vol and normalized slope as first-class, curve-auditable channels inside a neural return sensor rather than standalone overlays.
quote: The four features are chosen so each carries a distinct piece of market information: a one-bar return for momentum, RSI for the oscillator state, ATR divided by price for relative volatility, and the slope of a fast moving average for trend.

idea_name: Two-stage ATR dynamic high/low trend channel
mechanism: TR=max(H−L,|H−Cprev|,|L−Cprev|); pass1 Wilder RMA ATR(200); pass2 SMA(200) of RMA then ×0.8 as final ATR. Upper=SMA(high,InpLength)+ATR_final, Lower=SMA(low,InpLength)−ATR_final. Trend flips only on confirmed close cross of a boundary; trailing line uses lower band in uptrend / upper in downtrend; candles colored by state; arrows on state change offset by 2×ATR.
data_needed: OHLC; ATR_PERIOD=ATR_SMA_PERIOD=200; InpLength (default 10) for avg high/low.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic chart TF; any MT5 symbol with enough history for ~400+ bars warm-up.
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-adaptive channel regime with a slow double-smoothed ATR width and close-confirmed flips—MIS can read expand/contract envelope plus binary trend state.
quote: Rather than relying on fixed price levels, the indicator uses a smoothed Average True Range (ATR) calculation to create adaptive upper and lower channels that expand and contract as market conditions change.

idea_name: Close-crossing ATR channel as trend-transition event
mechanism: crossOver=(close[i−1]≤upper[i−1] && close[i]>upper[i]); crossUnder=(close[i−1]≥lower[i−1] && close[i]<lower[i]); only then flip persistent trend and emit arrow. Requires prior defined trend state so undefined warm-up bars do not signal.
data_needed: Prior/current channel buffers and closes; ATR for arrow offset.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same as channel indicator; chart-TF bars.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit bar-event change primitive tied to volatility-scaled boundaries, not a continuous oscillator cross.
quote: Arrows mark actual reversals because the indicator signals only when the trend state changes.

mechanism: Raw momentum=close[i]−close[i−InpLength]; HMA via WMA(half)−WMA(full) then WMA(sqrt(period)) on that intermediate; color/sign vs zero (above=positive momentum state, below=negative); gray fill to zero. Notes raw scale is instrument-dependent and flat markets produce frequent zero crosses.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/TF; magnitude not cross-comparable without normalization.
why_new_for_mis: Low-lag HMA-smoothed momentum polarity sensor for MIS directional-pressure context, with an explicit flat-market caution on zero crosses.
quote: Values above zero indicate a positive momentum state, while values below zero indicate a negative momentum state. A crossing of the zero line represents a change between these momentum states, but it should not be treated as a standalone entry signal, particularly during flat market conditions

mechanism: mid=(H+L)/2; raw bands=mid±ATR×multiplier; once trend established only the active band trails (ratchet: lower band only rises in bull, upper only falls in bear). Close through active band flips TREND_BULLISH/BEARISH, suppresses the opposite band with EMPTY_VALUE, and colors candles. Updates only on newly closed bars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H4 screenshot; chart PERIOD_CURRENT (any symbol/TF).
why_new_for_mis: Clean binary volatility-scaled trend state with documented buffers for EA consumption—classic Supertrend rebuilt as a non-repainting MIS regime tag.
quote: Given current volatility, is the market trending up or down right now?

idea_name: UT Bot ATR trailing-stop regime with EMA(1) flip signals
mechanism: LossDistance=ATR×multiplier; trailing stop ratchets (MathMax/MathMin) while price stays on one side, flips to opposite side on cross; trend state ±1 colors candles. Buy/sell when EMA(1) of source (close or Heikin Ashi close) crosses the stop with price on the same side. Non-repainting closed-bar updates; buffers expose signals, trend, trailing stop.
data_needed: ATR; optional Heikin Ashi close resource; atrPeriod/atrMultiplier (defaults 10, 1.5).
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-adjusted trailing-stop flip plus EMA crossover as a documented change/regime event stream for MIS automation (not just a visual TradingView port).
quote: These signals represent potential transitions between bullish and bearish market regimes.

mechanism: Additive or multiplicative seasonal_decompose: trend via centered moving average of period p; seasonal by arithmetic (additive) or geometric (multiplicative) mean of de-trended values over cycles; residual = y−T−S or y/(T·S). Indicators plot seasonal and residual components on chart TF.
data_needed: Price series (close etc.); period p; model additive|multiplicative (multiplicative requires strictly positive values).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic daily; AAPL PERIOD_D1 closes, period_=22 (~monthly), bars_total up to 10000.
why_new_for_mis: Splits price into trend vs recurring seasonal vs residual channels so MIS can sense cyclic structure and unexplained remainder separately from the raw series.
quote: Seasonal decomposition is a statistical technique used to break downtime series data into several components; Trend, Seasonality, and Residual.

idea_name: Decomposition residual structure as disruption flag
mechanism: After multiplicative monthly (p=22) decompose of AAPL daily closes, judge quality by residual mean≈1, small std, near-normal distribution, and white-noise look; visible residual spikes (e.g. 2020–2022 pandemic) flag periods when seasonal patterns are disrupted and should not be trusted.
data_needed: Residual vector from seasonal_decompose; optional distribution/mean/std diagnostics.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AAPL D1 case study; residual spike years 2020–2022 noted.
why_new_for_mis: Turns residual non-whiteness into a change/trust sensor: when seasonality breaks down, MIS can gate seasonal features off.
quote: Good decomposition: Residuals should look like random noise (white noise). Bad decomposition: Residuals still show visible structure (trends or seasonal effects that weren’t removed).

mechanism: Train Keras encoder→latent→decoder on MinMax-scaled OHLC (RELU hidden, sigmoid output, MSE); export encoder/decoder ONNX plus min/max bins; MQL5 indicator scales live OHLC, runs encode then decode, inverse-scales, and plots reconstructed candles (optional fill/hide originals). Latent+PCA path also discussed for dim reduction.
data_needed: Historical OHLC for train; ONNX encoder/decoder; MinMax min/max binaries; live OHLC bars.
why_new_for_mis: Neural noise-to-signal OHLC filter deployed live in MT5—MIS can sense a denoised price path or reconstruction residual vs raw bars.
quote: By trying to reconstruct the input data, the autoencoder learns essential features and removes noise or irrelevant information.

series_key: detecting structural breakpoints in price series using cusum in mql5
mechanism: r_t=log(C_t/C_{t−1}); z_t=(r_t−μ̂_{t−1})/σ̂_{t−1} from rolling W prior returns only (Bessel-corrected σ); S+=max(0,S++z−k), S−=min(0,S−+z+k); declare break when S+>h or S−<−h, then reset both to 0; refractory MinBarsBetweenBreaks; plot accumulators vs ±h and main-chart VLINEs. Persist S± via indicator buffers across ticks.
data_needed: Closes; W (default 100); k (0.50); h (4.0); refractory gap (10).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 demo attachment; designed cross-instrument via z-score standardization.
why_new_for_mis: Sequential, causal structural-break sensor that fires as evidence accumulates—unlike lagging fixed-window MA/ATR smoothers—giving MIS an online regime-change event stream.
quote: The method processes returns bar by bar, accumulates evidence of a distributional shift, and declares a breakpoint as soon as a statistical threshold is crossed.

series_key: detecting structural breakpoints in price series using cusum in mql5
idea_name: CUSUM as empirical volatility-regime detector gate
mechanism: 36-run battery (EURUSD/GBPUSD/XAUUSD/DE40/USTEC/USDJPY × M15/H1/H4 × P1 2021–23 / P2 2024–25) at W=100,k=0.50,h=4: mean ARL_emp≈65.7 vs Siegmund ARL0≈338 (~5× more alarms). F-test confirms variance shift in ~47% of breaks vs Welch mean shift ~0.7%. Quiet-vol tercile ARL≈430 (near theory). Use as vol-regime gate (resize/widen stops/pause mean-reversion), not directional entry; calibrate h empirically.
data_needed: Same CUSUM indicator stream; optional pre/post 200-bar F/t tests for validation.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, XAUUSD, DE40, USTEC, USDJPY on M15, H1, H4; macro-event latency table included.
why_new_for_mis: Evidence-backed reinterpretation: CUSUM breaks are primarily volatility-regime flags with known false-alarm inflation—MIS should consume them as vol gates with per-instrument empirical h, not mean-shift oracles.
quote: The CUSUM detector introduced in Part 1 is, empirically, a volatility regime detector, not a directional mean-shift detector.

series_key: developing a trading expert advisor from scratch
idea_name: Floating Chart Trade IDE UI plumbing
mechanism: Nested OBJ_CHART templates, event routing limits for objects inside charts, StageLocal floating-window helpers, IDE.tpl object recreation and drag/minimize positioning. Pure GUI/architecture for Chart Trade—no market feature, regime, or sensor math.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—floating-window and IDE object plumbing only.
quote: the biggest difficulty related to the use of the objects which we utilize in order to create the CHART TRADE interface in the floating window is that MetaTrader 5 is not really intended for this purpose.
